ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16600, promulgated November 26, 2019, as amended), together with its Enforcement Decree No. 30045, and the Financial Services Commission regulation on customer due diligence; Commercial Act provisions on corporate registration; Ministry of Government Legislation and Supreme Court registration rules for corporate registry certificates.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Company Registration (Certificate of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path exclusively (Republic of Korea is a Hague Apostille Convention state): notarization by a Korean notary public, then authentication certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, followed by attached Hague Apostille. Consular legalization is not applied because it is mutually exclusive and not required for Korea-origin documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Registry Information)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path exclusively: notarized copy issued by court registry office is certified by a Korean notary public, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea issues the Hague Apostille. No consular legalization step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing Incorporation Agent and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Organizing shareholders/board of directors of the entity, notarized in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path exclusively: original or notarized counterpart signed by directors is notarized by a Korean notary, then authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea with Hague Apostille attached. Consular legalization is not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Association (Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path exclusively: Articles of Association signed by all incorporators are notarized by a Korean notary, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea affixes the Hague Apostille. No consular legalization is required for Apostille Convention states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank where the company maintains or will maintain a corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path exclusively: bank officer signature and corporate seal certificate are authenticated by a Korean notary, followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea Hague Apostille. Consular legalization is not performed.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and OFAC non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists, European Union and United Kingdom financial sanctions lists, and the financial sanctions list published by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and the Financial Services Commission. For all proposed shareholders, directors, beneficial owners and senior managers, a risk-based customer due diligence protocol must include PEP identification, adverse media checks, nationality and residence risk scoring, source-of-funds documentation, and continuous transaction monitoring. Enhanced due diligence is required where any direct or indirect control nexus, high-risk jurisdiction, or unusual ownership structure is identified. Records must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) company name search and registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Korean Hangul script for the registered legal name. English names may be used as a foreign-language alias or trade name, typically adopted through phonetic transliteration. The four-tier naming convention requires (i) a distinctive brand or identifier, (ii) the legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa', (iii) a business purpose statement in the Articles of Association, and (iv) the registered office address. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered corporate name in the same registration district.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea (in a manner implying government sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a name rejection order, the applicant may file a written objection with the presiding registration judge of the District Court where the registry office is located, invoking the non-contentious registration procedure under the Korean civil procedure statutes. The judge must render a written decision within 7 days. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant may file an immediate appeal with the High Court. The applicant may simultaneously submit a revised name list containing first, second and third preferences, and request priority re-examination. The statutory filing fee for the objection is KRW 10,000; legal representation is recommended because registry judges apply strict similarity tests.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is formally permissible for initial registration under the Korean Commercial Act and court registry practice, but it is conditionally rejected by the National Tax Service and corporate banks in the Print-on-Demand online retail industry. The National Tax Service requires a demonstrable place of business for VAT and business registration purposes, and a virtual office may lead to assessment that the registered address is not the actual business site, causing tax notices and invoices to be sent to an address at which the company cannot physically receive them. Banks generally reject corporate current accounts when the sole registered office is a mail-forwarding venue, particularly for e-commerce merchants using online payment rails such as Stripe and PayPal, unless the company produces a fixed-term lease, evidence of local management presence and operational records. Therefore, a virtual office may be used only in the short term and should be upgraded to a serviced office lease before bank account onboarding and tax registration confirmation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: moderate, approximately 30-40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first year of operation for a POD online retail entity. Checklist for inspection: (1) visible corporate signage at the registered address; (2) operating equipment, samples, packaging or inventory; (3) staff presence and payroll records; (4) order management and sales records; (5) VAT invoices consistent with declared business; (6) display of required business information on the online shopfront in accordance with the E-Commerce Act. The National Tax Service, local municipal tax inspectors and court registry personnel may conduct unannounced visits under the Framework Act on National Taxes; failure to substantiate the registered place of business may lead to cancellation of business registration, immediate VAT sanctions and bank account freezing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) provisions at Articles 287-2 through 287-74; specifically Article 287-5 on contents of the Articles of Incorporation, Article 287-11 on registration of establishment, Article 287-25 on payment of contributions and liability of directors, together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident investors and the Local Tax Act for registration and education surtaxes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registry Office with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; foreign investment preliminary reporting is handled through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest KOREA via the Foreign Investment Support System (FISS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Charter) executed by all incorporators, together with the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company, the subscription list, minutes of the first board resolution, and evidence of paid-in contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None, no statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, at least part of each contribution must be paid or delivered to the initial directors before registration, and the amounts received must be deposited in a bank account in the name of the company under formation or a provisional subscription account. The deposit certificate is required by the registry court and the funds become unrestricted company assets after successful incorporation registration. A typical practical working capital for an e-commerce LLC is KRW 10,000,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FORMAL PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF KR YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

WHEREAS, KR YUHANGHOESA has been incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea as a limited liability company and is authorized to conduct retail sale via mail order houses or internet, including print-on-demand custom merchandise retailing; and

WHEREAS, the initial directors have reviewed the Articles of Incorporation, the subscription list, the certificate of deposit, and the documents supporting the opening of the company’s bank account; and

WHEREAS, the board of directors is vested with authority under the Articles of Incorporation and applicable Korean law to adopt resolutions concerning the subscription of contributions, banking arrangements, the registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. The initial capital contributions described in the Articles of Incorporation are hereby ratified, fully subscribed, and allotted to each member in accordance with the subscription list. The board acknowledges that each member’s contributions, whether in cash or non-cash assets, have been paid or delivered as required by the Commercial Act, and the directors’ obligation to deposit the received amounts is confirmed as completed.

2. Banking Authorization. The board hereby designates the bank named in the corporate formation record as the principal deposit bank of the company. Each initial director, acting jointly or severally as authorized by the corporate seal policy, is authorized to open, maintain, operate, and close corporate bank accounts, execute banking mandates, endorse negotiable instruments, initiate wire transfers, enroll in electronic banking channels, and take any other action necessary for the treasury and payment operations of the company.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office set forth in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the company’s legal seat. The board directs the managing director, or a designated formation agent, to file all statutory notices, lease certificates, and registry amendments necessary to maintain the accuracy of the registered address with the District Court Registry Office and the National Tax Service.

The company’s registered office is the official address for service of legal process, tax assessments, and government correspondence.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The board appoints the individual identified in the formation dossier as Managing Director / Representative Member and grants that individual full authority to execute contracts, sign tax filings, open banking relationships, supervise employees, and represent the company in dealings with third parties. The board also appoints the individual identified as Auditor if an auditor is required by law, with supervisory powers in accordance with Articles 287-31 through 287-34 of the Commercial Act.

5. Delegation and Continuing Authority. The managing director is authorized to engage attorneys, certified public accountants, tax agents, corporate secretarial services, and licensed labor advisors as needed to implement this resolution and to perform all actions reasonably required to commence the company’s business operations. Any transaction exceeding the authority threshold set by a subsequent board resolution shall require prior board approval.

ADOPTED by the unanimous written consent of the initial directors, effective as of the date of signing, and may be executed in counterparts. This resolution is binding on all officers and may be shown to banks, courts, government agencies, and counterparties as evidence of corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Foreign Investment Notification and Capital Escrow Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest KOREA through the Foreign Investment Support System (FISS) or a designated domestic foreign exchange bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A non-resident individual or corporate investor must submit a foreign investment report pursuant to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or on the date the subscription payment is made. The report must be filed electronically through FISS or accepted by a designated foreign exchange bank, and it must disclose the investor’s nationality, investment amount, remittance route, intended business purpose, and shareholding percentage. After acceptance, KOTRA or the bank issues a certificate of foreign investment notification. The capital sought to be contributed must be remitted from the investor’s overseas account to a provisional subscription account opened in the name of the company under formation. Since there is no minimum legal capital, the stated capital can be set in the Articles of Incorporation at an amount sufficient to cover initial registration fees, office deposits, and operating overhead.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport or corporate certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Power of attorney or signed formation agent engagement letter
Foreign investment report form
Bank wire transfer instruction and remittance statement
Statement of planned business purpose and proposed paid-in capital amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is returned or rejected, the applicant must correct the inaccurate investor identity data or remittance source and refile through FISS within five business days. If a foreign exchange bank declines to accept the report due to incomplete ownership documentation, submit a notarized English translation of the Articles of Incorporation, the investor’s identification, and the executed power of attorney to the bank’s compliance desk to cure the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Subscription List
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean notary public affiliated with the Korean Notary Association, selected by the formation agent or the foreign investor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must prepare and finalize the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, statement of limited liability, business purpose, registered office location, total value of contributions, method of contribution, names and addresses of directors, auditor provisions if any, and the company’s public notice method. All incorporators must sign or seal the original Articles, and each member’s name and subscription amount must be listed in a separate subscription list. The notary must verify the legal capacity, identity, and signatures of all participants, confirm that no purpose is unlawful, and notarize the Articles. For non-resident incorporators, foreign execution abroad must be legalized by apostille or consular authentication before submission to the notary. The notarized Articles become a mandatory exhibit for registry court filing, and any change after execution requires a formal amendment process.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in English or Korean translation
Subscription list of all members with amounts
Passports or professional identification of all incorporators
Written acceptance forms from initial directors and auditor
Power of attorney for the Korean formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify the Articles because the corporate name conflicts with an existing registered trade name, conduct a new name availability search through the Supreme Court Registry System and execute an amended Articles with a revised name. If a non-resident signature is rejected, obtain consular legalization or apostille on the personal signature and resubmit the Articles to the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Contributions and Issuance of Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank operating in South Korea, such as a major domestic bank or a designated foreign exchange bank authorized to open provisional corporate subscription accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following notarization, the initial directors must open a provisional subscription account in the company’s intended legal name and require each member to transfer the agreed contribution amount into that account. The deposit must remain in the account until the incorporation registration is completed, and the bank must issue an official certificate of deposit or balance confirmation in the company’s name. This certificate is an indispensable exhibit for the court registration because the registry must confirm that directors received payment before applying for registration. If a member contributes non-cash assets such as machinery, intellectual property, software, or inventory, a licensed appraiser must prepare an in-kind contribution valuation report and the board must confirm the valuation. The bank deposit and the in-kind valuation records must correspond exactly with the amounts stated in the Articles of Incorporation to avoid registration queries.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of foreign investment notification or domestic remittance record
Application for provisional subscription account opening
Company seal or newly prepared corporate seal certificate
Director identification documents and registered agent confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds issuance of the deposit certificate because the foreign remittance does not match the reported investment amount, the investor must provide a corrected remittance advice or request the bank to issue a currency conversion certificate. If the subscription account is rejected because the company is not yet registered, the bank may instead use a trustee or escrow arrangement with a licensed commercial bank, and the escrow release letter must be submitted to the registry office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, or the Supreme Court Registry Information System electronic filing portal for authorized agents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the directors receive the contributions, the representative member or authorized formation agent must file the application for registration of establishment with the registry court. The application must include the company’s exact name, registered office address, business purpose, total contributed capital, member liability limitation, director names, and auditor names if applicable. The notarized Articles of Incorporation, deposit certificate, subscription list, director consent forms, and any required power of attorney must be attached. If the company is a foreign-invested entity, the foreign investment report certificate or a copy accepted by KOTRA must also be submitted to verify compliance. The court examines the application, publishes the registration in the official registry, and upon acceptance issues a certificate of authenticated registration, at which point the company becomes a valid legal entity separate from its members.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and subscription list
Certificate of paid-in capital or deposit balance certificate
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Consent forms of initial directors and auditor
Corporate seal certificate and underlying identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary order to correct a defect, the formation agent must respond within the court-specified period, normally two weeks, through the electronic filing system. If the registration period lapses, the applicant must file a new registration application, pay the official fee again, and attach an updated deposit certificate and notarized Articles to cure the expired filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Tax Registration, and Operating Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office; parallel registration with local municipal tax office and the relevant social insurance authorities for any employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No later than twenty days after the date of incorporation registration, the representative director must file a business registration application with the National Tax Service. The application must list the principal place of business, company name, corporate registration number, representative identity, and the appropriate Korean Standard Industrial Classification corresponding to ISIC 4791 retail sale via mail order or internet. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate and assign a corporate tax identification number for value-added tax, corporate income tax, and withholding tax obligations. Because the business involves print-on-demand custom apparel, the company must also prepare to issue electronic tax invoices for sales to Korean taxpayers and comply with annual financial statement filing requirements for corporate entities. If the company hires employees, it must register with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance authorities before payroll commencement. After the business registration certificate is issued, the company may activate the operating corporate bank account and connect payment gateways such as Stripe or PayPal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of authenticated incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Certificate of corporate seal
Copy of registered office lease agreement
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
Identity documents and financial statement templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service queries the registered office because the premises appear residential, the company must submit the registered office lease agreement, a safety inspection document for the building, and a utility bill in the company’s name within ten business days. If the business registration is suspended for an incomplete tax code classification, the formation agent can amend the application and resubmit online without requiring a new court registration, provided that the legal entity remains validly registered.'}

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – the entity is a digital-facing online retail operator under ISIC 4791 and does not own or operate any factory, chemical assembly line, or industrial warehouse in South Korea. No industrial licensing authority is applicable to the company’s own premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for the company’s online retail sale of print-on-demand custom apparel. Any physical fulfillment activity is performed by third-party print-on-demand suppliers in their own jurisdictions, and those suppliers bear responsibility for their own manufacturing licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – Exempt; no Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration tier is triggered because the company will not operate physical facilities with discharge points, emission stacks, or waste treatment systems.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, combustion emissions, or hazardous waste handling activities will be conducted by the entity in Korea. If the company later acquires a physical print shop or warehouse, it must re-evaluate under the Act on Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control, the Clean Air Conservation Act, and the Water Environment Conservation Act, and install measured pollution prevention equipment before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – Civil Defense fire certification under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems Act, structural load inspection, and factory workplace safety approval are not required for an office-only e-commerce retail entity with no physical inventory storage. The company must, however, satisfy the general occupational safety duties under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office workers, including providing safety training and complying with workplace stress and ergonomic standards, and must prepare a written workplace safety plan when it regularly employs five or more workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) in South Korea, the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the Business Registration Number (사업자등록번호). The procurement procedure is as follows: (1) Prepare the required documents, including the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, a copy of the foreign entity's registration certificate, the passport of the foreign director or legal representative, and a power of attorney if a local agent is appointed. (2) Submit the application to the district tax office (세무서) having jurisdiction over the registered place of business in Korea, or file electronically via the HomeTax portal. (3) The NTS will review the application and issue the Business Registration Certificate, which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number. (4) For VAT purposes, the entity must also complete a VAT registration application (부가가치세 사업자등록) if it will make taxable supplies; this is typically integrated into the business registration process. (5) The entity must also register for the electronic tax invoice system (전자세금계산서) through HomeTax to comply with mandatory e-invoicing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No threshold; mandatory registration for any taxable business activity (including foreign entities with a Korean place of business)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) for all B2B transactions, issued and transmitted in real-time via the HomeTax system. The system requires API integration for automated issuance and includes anti-fraud digital stamping (전자서명) to ensure authenticity. Non-compliance results in penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including print-on-demand custom apparel) are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act, provided the goods are physically exported from South Korea and the exporter retains evidence of export. Qualifying offshore digital services are also zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident and consumed outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (외화획득증명) or Foreign Exchange Earned Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the zero-rating is claimed without proper substantiation or if the foreign exchange is not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, the NTS will impose additional VAT at 10% plus an additional tax of 40% of the unpaid amount. Fraudulent claims may result in criminal penalties, including fines up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment up to 5 years, along with retrospective clawback of all zero-rated benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) via the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; operational FX oversight is delegated to the Bank of Korea and the Korea Customs Service for trade-related foreign exchange declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current account and capital account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, yet the system retains procedural friction rather than blanket prohibitions. The Korean won (KRW) is freely convertible for current account transactions such as trade settlements, service fees, and profit remittances, subject to mandatory reporting through designated foreign exchange banks when transaction amounts exceed USD 500,000 or the KRW equivalent of 500 million won for cross-border settlements. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment inbound equity injections, foreign currency loans, and overseas direct investments, require prior notification or license from the Bank of Korea or the delegated foreign exchange bank, though approval is generally granted without substantive restriction for compliant structures. Export proceeds must be surrendered or deposited into a foreign exchange bank account within a statutory period, typically within 18 months from the date of export declaration, and exporters are required to convert foreign currency receipts into KRW as part of the settlement process unless a waiver is obtained for operational purposes. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after corporate tax settlement and are subject to withholding tax of 22 percent (including resident surtax) unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty, and the remitting bank requires evidence of tax payment, audited financial statements, and board resolution approving the dividend. For a private limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) engaged in print-on-demand retailing with transactions routed through Stripe and PayPal, the practical challenge lies not in convertibility refusal but in the banks' insistence on underlying documentary evidence that each remittance corresponds to real service or trade activity, preventing the appearance of disguised loan repayments or capital flight. The overall assessment classifies Korea as an OECD member with high capital mobility, but compliance with reporting thresholds, settlement timelines, and tax clearance certificates remains mandatory; failure to observe these procedures can result in administrative fines and delayed repatriation of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must file an electronic export declaration with the Korea Customs Service and receive foreign currency proceeds into a designated foreign exchange bank account within 18 months from the export declaration date. The proceeds must be either converted into Korean won or deposited in foreign currency with a licensed bank; if conversion is elected, the bank applies the standard market rate and reports to the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. No mandatory percentage conversion ratio applies, as the regime permits exporters to retain foreign currency in designated accounts, but all foreign exchange transactions must be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and accompanied by the exporter's Foreign Exchange Transaction confirmation and underlying trade documents such as commercial invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR)
Capital Escrow Account for paid-in capital verification and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account for POD trade disbursements
Basic Operational Currency Account with cross-border remittance and FX hedging desk
Basic Operational Currency Account for SME exporters

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex have limited legal viability as primary corporate bank accounts for a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mandates that all cross-border capital flows and trade settlements be channeled through domestic licensed foreign exchange banks or entities registered with the Financial Services Commission (FSC). While these EMIs can be used as downstream payment aggregation tools for collecting customer payments from Stripe and PayPal, they cannot serve as the statutory settlement account for capital account transactions, dividend remittances, or export proceeds surrender. Furthermore, the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) applies strong anti-money laundering scrutiny to corporations that route significant sales through unregistered foreign payment intermediaries, which may trigger enhanced due diligence and potential reporting to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). A hybrid architecture is advised: the Yuhan Hoesa should maintain a primary KRW and USD account at Shinhan Bank or Kookmin Bank for statutory trade settlement, tax payments, and capital verification, while using licensed payment gateways that have local partnerships with Korean acquiring banks for daily e-commerce settlement. Pure offshore EMI concentration is incompatible with the statutory requirement that any transaction exceeding USD 5,000 in foreign exchange must be reported with a purpose code through a licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) are generally required to appear physically in-branch for initial corporate account opening under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 10 and the FSC's Regulation on Financial Transactions. However, major Korean banks including Shinhan, Kookmin, and Hana allow remote opening for foreign-invested entities through consular notarization and video-based interview, provided that the foreign director holds a valid Alien Registration Certificate or presents a notarized power of attorney to a local resident representative. For a Yuhan Hoesa with foreign shareholding, the mandatory KYC protocol demands in-branch or video interview with a senior compliance officer to verify the identity of signatories, confirm the beneficial ownership structure, and sign the Foreign Exchange Transaction Agreement. Without a resident director, remote consular proxy opening is permitted if the local representative presents a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, passport copies, certificate of incorporation, and the board resolution authorizing the account opening, along with a certificate of real office address in Korea. Banks uniformly reject non-face-to-face opening for UBOs residing in high-risk jurisdictions or when the corporate registry data fails to match the beneficial ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) shareholding obscurity in the Korean corporate registry: the bank's screening may flag a foreign investor who holds over 25 percent of equity without transparent chain-of-title records or when the investor is a shell holding in a non-disclosed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and apostilled group structure chart illustrating the full ownership cascade to natural persons; certified copy of the corporate registry extract (deungsabon) from the Korean courts; passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; a certificate of incorporation and good standing certificates from the foreign parent's registry; signed director and UBO declaration (Form for Financial Transactions, Korea); and a clear written narrative explaining sources of wealth and source of funds for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared business activity (POD retailing under ISIC 4791) and the payment settlement profile dominated by digital platforms (Stripe and PayPal), which may indicate unlicensed e-money handling or third-party payment aggregation without a required license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act (EFTA).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal business description including the operational workflow for POD manufacturing and direct-to-consumer shipping; executed master service agreements with Stripe Payments Korea Ltd. and PayPal Pte. Ltd.; platform settlement statements demonstrating that funds are collected on behalf of the company and remitted net of gateway fees; a compliance opinion confirming that the POD model does not involve storing customer funds or conducting electronic money issuance; and the company's internal AML policy aligning with the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border transaction patterns envisioned as high-volume, low-ticket international sales from consumers in Southeast Asia, the US, and Europe, which may be misclassified by the bank as a potential money laundering or trade-based laundering risk due to lack of physical logistics evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-file bundle containing invoices, proof of fulfillment by the POD supplier, shipping tracking numbers, carrier bills of lading or postal receipts, and export declaration numbers from the Korea Customs Service; reconciliation reports mapping declared transactions to receipts from payment gateways; subscription or order-level data from the e-commerce platform proving the genuine nature of each sale; and a certified audit trail showing that the company's gross margin aligns with market norms for apparel retailing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder into the Yuhan Hoesa could trigger enhanced scrutiny for violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting thresholds or suspicious commingling of investment capital with operational revenue in the same account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign direct investment notification certificate (per the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if applied) or the correspondent bank's Foreign Exchange Transaction confirmation; a board resolution for the capital increase; a bank-issued Foreign Currency Deposit Receipt evidencing the inward remittance with a purpose code of 'Investment Capital'; the corporate tax payment schedule and a certified copy of the shareholders' remittance instructions; and signed statutory declarations from all directors that the capital is not derived from offshore criminal proceeds, corroborated by source-of-wealth statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an inbound equity or shareholder loan injection, the remittance must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank with a clear purpose code corresponding to 'Investment Capital' under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting regimen. The sending bank should transmit via SWIFT MT103 to the Yuhan Hoesa's capital escrow account at Shinhan Bank or Kookmin Bank, naming the actual investor as the remitter and the Korean entity's account as the beneficiary. The remittance instruction must reference the 'Foreign Investment Notification Certificate' if the investor is a foreign national and the entity is registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, or otherwise a Foreign Exchange Transaction confirmation for a domestic loan from a group company. Upon crediting, the beneficiary bank conducts capital verification, and the certificate should be issued by the bank showing the inflow date, amount, and FX rate applied. The KRW conversion of the foreign currency contribution must be executed at the bank's market rate, with the bank reporting the transaction to the Bank of Korea and retaining a copy of the Korean Customs Service's foreign investment declaration. The funds must remain in the dedicated capital account until the paid-in capital is registered in the commercial registry and the court's registration certificate is updated, balancing the need for operational liquidity against the statutory verification timeline.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements involving payments to foreign POD manufacturers, shipping carriers, and marketing service providers, the company should use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, documentary collections for modest-value supplier drafts, and commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) only for bulk procurement from vendors requiring contractual payment security. When remitting from the Shinhan Bank or Woori Bank operational account, the company must submit an export/import declaration to the Korea Customs Service for physical goods movements and a Foreign Exchange Transaction confirmation specifying the purpose code (e.g., 'Service Payment', 'Trade Payment', or 'Overseas Direct Investment') if the disbursement is for business expansion. For recurring disbursements to print-on-demand suppliers outside Korea, the bank will apply its automated screening against the FSC sanctions list and the UN Security Council resolutions; the company must pre-register the supplier names, country, and invoice templates with the compliance team. All outbound SWIFT messages must include accurate beneficiary bank identifiers (BIC/IBAN) and reference the underlying trade invoice and contract number to avoid delay or rejection. The company is advised to maintain separate USD and EUR sub-accounts to minimize conversion fees and to centralize disbursement approvals under dual-signature authority in the board resolution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX Contracts: The Yuhan Hoesa may enter plain-vanilla USD/KRW or EUR/KRW deliverable forward contracts with a licensed Korean commercial bank up to 100 percent of anticipated export proceeds or payment obligations evidenced by pending invoices, provided that the underlying trade exposure is documented and the bank files a Foreign Exchange Transaction declaration.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): The Bank of Korea restricts onshore NDF trading between domestic banks and non-residents; however, the Yuhan Hoesa may hedge KRW exposure through NDFs with offshore counterparties only if arranged through a Korean bank's offshore branch, while maintaining strict underlying exposure documentation and compliance with the Foreign Exchange Transaction Act notification requirements.

Currency Swaps: Cross-currency interest rate swaps and plain FX swaps are permissible only for the purpose of managing trade-related cash flow mismatches or matching the currency profile of outstanding foreign currency loans; the bank will require a board resolution, a certified trade forecast, and prior notification to the Bank of Korea for notional amounts exceeding KRW 5 billion. Speculative hedging without an underlying operational exposure is strictly prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and approval of annual financial statements (Korean: sawon chonghoe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; minutes and resolutions retained at the registered office in Korea and available for inspection by the competent district court, National Tax Service, and Financial Supervisory Service upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or preserve meeting minutes is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 2,000,000 under the Commercial Act; no automatic strike-off exists, but non-approval of financial statements may trigger tax filing penalties and lender/agent covenant defaults.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value-Added Tax (VAT) return and electronic tax invoice filing for POD retail sales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (1 January to 30 June) filed by 25 July; second half (1 July to 31 December) filed by 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-declaration triggers NTS additional taxes of up to 10% of unpaid VAT plus daily overdue interest of 0.022%; chronic non-filing may lead to compulsory business registration closure and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and accompanying financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, no later than 31 March of the following year; legally due within three months of the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, failure to file attracts an additional tax of 20% of the understated or unreported corporate income tax; under-reporting attracts 10%; overdue amounts accrue at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum). Persistent non-payment can lead to compulsory collection, seizure of assets, and criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (Korean: beop-in jibang sodukse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City, county, or district tax authority via the local tax Wetax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, no later than 30 April of the following year; legally due within four months of the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing under the Local Tax Collection Act attracts an additional tax of up to 20% of the unpaid local corporate income tax plus statutory overdue interest; continued non-payment may result in compulsory collection from corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Management Report and UBO/foreign equity confirmation (conditional where any foreign investor holds 10% or more of the Yuhan Hoesa membership interests)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report due by 31 March following the fiscal year-end within 90 days; any transfer of foreign-owned membership interests must be reported within 30 days from the date of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or a false filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 2,000,000 and may result in loss of foreign-invested company status, registration benefits, and tax incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Report on Foreign Financial Accounts, including PayPal, Stripe, and foreign bank account balances held outside Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the following year if the aggregate balance of foreign financial accounts exceeded KRW 500,000,000 (approximately USD 357,000) at any month-end during the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported or falsely reported foreign accounts are subject to a penalty of up to 20% of the unreported balance, criminal prosecution, and compulsory collection; there is no administrative strike-off, but the tax office may seize assets and suspend the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements (conditional on mandatory audit thresholds being met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) external audit information system; audited statements also presented to members at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual members' meeting, in any event within three months of the balance-sheet date (by 31 March for a calendar-year entity); the auditor must submit the audit report to the FSS within 14 days after the audit report date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies etc., non-audit or submission failure can result in imprisonment up to three years and/or a fine up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 36,000), plus FSS corrective orders and administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register and records audit / corporate secretarial confirmation covering register of members, register of directors, register of charges or mortgages, minute book, and accounting vouchers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; records maintained at the registered office and made available for inspection by the National Tax Service, Financial Supervisory Service, KOTRA, and competent district court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April following each fiscal year-end; immediately upon any change of directors, members, registered office, or security interests over company assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete statutory registers violate the Commercial Act and expose directors to administrative fines up to KRW 2,000,000 and civil liability for loss caused by false registration; material amendments must additionally be recorded with the local district court within two weeks.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies etc., a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint an independent CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants if total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end are KRW 12,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 8.6 million at KRW 1,400/USD). The mandatory audit requirement also applies without regard to the asset threshold if the company is a public company listed on the Korea Exchange or otherwise designated as a public company under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. A company with total assets of KRW 100,000,000,000 or more must additionally adopt an internal accounting management system, use Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, and appoint an audit committee. Revenue and headcount are not separate statutory bright-line triggers for a Korean LLC, but a bank, investor, parent company, or procurement counterparty may independently require an audit; the Financial Supervisory Service may also designate a company for external audit based on group-wide size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa, Korean GAAP is the default accounting framework; K-IFRS is mandatory for listed companies, financial institutions, designated large unlisted companies, and any entity that has voluntarily adopted K-IFRS. Mandatory audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA) by an independent CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a central public UBO registry for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa limited liability companies. The company must maintain a current register of members at its registered office in Korea, and any transfer of membership interests must be reflected in that register to be opposable to the company and to third parties. Where a foreign investor holds 10% or more of the equity or voting rights, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act imposes both an annual Foreign Investment Management Report due by 31 March and a change report to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of any shareholding or membership transfer. The register, minute book, and supporting corporate records must be physically available in Korea for inspection by tax authorities, the Financial Supervisory Service, KOTRA, and the competent court.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of member and director resolutions
Financial statements, tax filings, and statutory audit reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 900 per year for a Korean registered office and local corporate secretarial compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a mandatory Korean statutory audit; USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 per year for a voluntary audit of a smaller non-threshold POD entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-21% progressive national Corporate Income Tax on taxable income (KRW 0-200 million: 9%; KRW 200 million-20 billion: 19%; over KRW 20 billion: 21%), plus a 10% Local Income Tax surcharge that yields an aggregate headline top marginal rate of 23.1%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Yuhan Hoesa (domestic limited liability company) is taxed on worldwide income. Incentives applicable to a POD retail entity include: (i) R&D tax credits up to 25% for qualifying technology development expenses; (ii) SME and venture tax deductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; (iii) preferential foreign-invested enterprise tax holidays for capital goods imported for qualifying high-tech foreign direct investment, but not for ordinary retail/warehousing; (iv) foreign tax credit for Korean tax paid on foreign-source income where the entity is actually controlled and managed in Korea; Korea does not operate an OECD patent box for e-commerce or apparel trade

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official filing form: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement (Corporate Income Tax Return Form 1). Electronic filing is mandatory via the HomeTax e-filing portal of the National Tax Service, using the standard return package with attachments for financial statements, tax base reconciliation, and withholding/tax credit schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a semi-annual interim corporate income tax prepayment declaration for the first six months of the accounting period. For a December 31 year-end, the interim return is due by August 31 and the final annual return is due by March 31 of the following year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months from the close of the fiscal year under Article 60(2) of the Corporate Income Tax Act. If the fiscal year ends on December 31, the filing deadline is March 31 of the immediately following year; approved extensions for statutory audit or consolidated tax return situations are granted for up to one month or 45 days, respectively

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Legal entity identification and business registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Yuhan Hoesa's corporate number, business place address, representative director, and place of effective management (POEM) in Korea
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an entity owned by non-resident shareholders, state the full name and identification number of each non-resident director/member, and disclose whether the POEM is in Korea. If overseas founders make all commercial decisions and sign e-commerce platform contracts offshore, the NTS can recharacterize the Korean entity as a foreign entity or PE; complete this box with actual operational substance and board minutes reflecting Korean management control

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Fiscal year and settlement of accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commerce period, settlement date, financial statements, balance sheet, income statement, and annual revenue including gross POD merchandise sales and shipping fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net Stripe, PayPal, or other payment processor charges against gross sales. Show gross proceeds in Box 2 revenue and separately deduct processing fees as distribution expenses with merchant statements. If the PayPal/Stripe settlement accounts are domiciled offshore, attach the original bank and payment processor statements to avoid a hidden foreign income assertion

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-taxable income and tax-exempt adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Post-tax dividend income that is excluded under the dividend-received deduction, capital gains that are rolled over, and other non-taxable reserve releases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A POD apparel merchant ordinarily will have no non-taxable income; do not include digital platform cost reimbursements as non-taxable unless the reimbursement is a true cost pass-through from the customer. Record all chargebacks and refunds as sales deductions supported by refund vouchers, not as non-taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, print-on-demand production costs, e-commerce marketplace fees, payment processing charges, shipping and delivery costs, marketing, IT/web subscriptions, depreciation of POD equipment, rent, salaries, and statutory welfare contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges from a foreign print supplier or design IP licensor must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be evidenced by contracts and transfer pricing documentation; otherwise the NTS can disregard the deduction and impose a 10%-40% unfaithful return penalty. Unsubstantiated payments to a non-resident related party may be reclassified as dividends and trigger 22% withholding

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable income before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue less total deductible expenses, plus non-taxable adjustments, minus reserve items, computed in the statutory tax base reconciliation statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity sells apparel globally through foreign online channels, allocate revenue according to the place where the Korean company carries on business; revenue cannot be allocated to an offshore headquarter service provider that performs no purchasing, quality, or inventory functions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Net operating loss carryforward deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses incurred in prior years that are deductible in the current year; the statutory carryforward period is 10 years for eligible losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-controlled Korean LLC cannot use the losses of its foreign shareholders or sister companies; only the Korean entity's own statutory tax losses after full compliance with the Corporate Tax Act are deductible. Losses cannot be shifted by transfer pricing adjustments from a related foreign manufacturer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable income and computed tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after NOL deduction; computed national Corporate Income Tax using the 9%, 19%, and 21% progressive brackets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the local income tax surcharge schedule as additional tax required with the national return. The applicable tax rates are calculated on the Korean tax base; no foreign tax credit is available for payments to a related party that are not legally a foreign income tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, job creation/increased employment credits, and tax on foreign-source income paid to Korea
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim a foreign tax credit, retain the foreign tax assessment and proof of actual payment; if non-resident shareholders received dividends from the Korean entity, their foreign residence tax is not creditable in Korea and does not reduce the Korean withholding or local income tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Aggregate tax, withholding, interim payments, and net tax due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed national Corporate Income Tax less tax credits, minimum tax rates, interim prepayment paid, withholding credits, plus penalties; net national Corporate Income Tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a non-resident shareholder or third party paid domestic withholding tax on behalf of the LLC, the certificate must be attached; otherwise the company will be assessed for the full CIT without credit. The net corporate tax payable is the sum that can become a joint and several liability of the representative director if unpaid and the company has insufficient assets

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Non-resident related-party payment reconciliation and withholding schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule listing dividends, interest, technical service fees, royalties, and other payments remitted to non-residents, with the domestic WHT amount and any treaty-reduced rate claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach for every cross-border payment: the written agreement, the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a beneficial ownership declaration, and the treaty-article position. Payments made without a TRC after the distribution date cannot apply the reduced treaty rate and the entity may be jointly liable for the 22% withholding plus penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Transfer pricing documentation schedule and CIGA substance statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of intercompany transactions, aggregate amounts with foreign related parties, the selected transfer pricing method, and the economic substance/CIGA location of the POD business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must identify whether the core income-generating activities (procurement, inventory risk, customer contracting, and software service) are performed in Korea. If a foreign parent prints shirts and sells to Korean retail customers, determine whether the foreign entity has a Korean PE due to contracting activities; for dividend repatriation, the schedule must prove that the Korean entity has real staff and assets, otherwise the NTS may apply tax anti-abuse rules to deny treaty benefits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers an unfaithful return penalty equal to 20% of the underpaid tax for a non-fraudulent failure and 40% for fraudulent omission; under-reported taxable income attracts a 10%-30% error penalty, and unpaid national tax attracts daily overdue charges (currently generally 0.025% per day on the unpaid national tax, subject to a statutory maximum). A person who intentionally omits revenue or submits false invoices may face criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; the court may impose imprisonment for up to two years, or a fine of not more than twice the tax evaded, for basic tax fraud; if the amount of tax evaded is economically substantial, the Specific Economic Crimes Aggravated Punishment Act can produce aggravated imprisonment plus large fines. The NTS may also issue a tax delinquent designation, which includes a travel ban (departure restriction) and refusal to issue or renew certificates until the tax liabilities are settled.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate absent a tax treaty: 20% national withholding tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act on non-resident dividends plus 2% Local Income Tax surcharge (10% of the 20% national WHT). The effective tax rate on an outbound dividend is therefore 22% of the gross distribution; a tax treaty may reduce the national portion (e.g. 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the beneficiary's residence and shareholding)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before distribution or payment, the foreign beneficial owner must submit to the Korean paying company: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the resident tax authority, (ii) the applicable DTA article and ownership percentage, and (iii) a Beneficial Ownership Statement evidencing that the recipient is the economic owner and has no abusive conduit arrangement. The Korean payer must retain the original or certified copy of the TRC and record the treaty-reduced rate on the withholding schedule in HomeTax. If the Korean payer withholds at the domestic 22% rate, the non-resident recipient may file a refund claim with the N
